questions.title: Will Russia officially announce a new mobilisation of reservists by 31 October 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 and 31 Oct 2026 (Moscow time) a presidential decree or an official announcement by the Russian president or government declares a mobilisation (partial or general) of reservists, as published on kremlin.ru / pravo.gov.ru or reported by two major wire services. Regular conscription, contract recruitment, regional quotas, reservist training call-ups (BARS, special musters) and summonses for 'record checks' do not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: reference class = declared mobilisations during the current war, 1 (Sep 2022) in 4.6 years, Poisson with +0.5 smoothing over 22 days. signals: LR 1.3 mobilisation risk index 54 'elevated' (legal readiness 62, rising); LR 0.8 the rumoured post-election '1 October window' passed with no decree; LR 0.8 the state keeps substituting (quotas, foreigners, coercion of conscripts) and recruitment is only ~10% below 2025; official denials taken as LR 1.0 (they preceded 2022 too).

history.reason: Pre-mortem (it is 31 Oct and I was wrong): a sudden front collapse or a decision already taken behind closed doors; neither story has visible evidence now. Opening: no battlefield shock of the 2022 Kharkiv kind; the index is elevated but the substitutes are working.

MRI 14 Oct: 55, unchanged. 17 days left, base rate shrinks with the window. Signals: Kluge's September data shows recruitment steady at ~1,000/day (29.9k, -6% y/y), no decree, no mass summons to reservists, no exit ban; the energy-truce channel slightly lowers motive (LR 0.95); Kluge's argument that 'privatized coercion' could push the Kremlin to mobilise to regain control is a longer-run factor (LR 1.0 within 17 days).

MRI 18 Oct: 55, unchanged. 13 days left: the base rate shrinks with the window. Evidence both ways is weak: the energy truce collapsed and Putin (16 Oct) ruled out concessions (LR 1.15), while Kluge and Massicot (RFE/RL 16 Oct) see steady recruitment and no emergent manpower deficit (LR 0.9). No decree, no mass summons to reservists, no exit closure.

questions.title: Will Russia legally bar reservists as a category from leaving the country by 30 June 2027?
questions.criteria: YES if by 30 Jun 2027 a Russian federal law, presidential decree or government decree enters into force that restricts departure abroad for men in the military reserve as a category (for example all reservists of certain ages or ranks), without an individual summons or call-up order having been served. Restrictions that apply only to men already served a summons, to conscripts, or to specific professions with state secrets do not count. Source: pravo.gov.ru text plus two major outlets. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: no category-wide exit ban for reservists in 4.6 years of war despite 2022 pressure; 0 events, +0.5 smoothing, 264 days. signals: LR 1.2 legal readiness component at 62 and rising (summons register with restrictions, notary-chamber letter on reservists aged 18-30, Sep 2026); LR 1.2 garrison court cases for unauthorised absence rising (my court collector).

history.reason: Opening: the legal machinery for individual restrictions exists; a category-wide ban is a political step not yet visible.

questions.title: Will the presidential decree expanding Russian military police search powers be signed by 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 30 Nov 2026 Russia's president signs the decree drafted by the Ministry of Defence (published for discussion around 8 Oct 2026) that gives the military police inquiry powers and search measures (cordons, ambushes, fingerprinting of detainees without documents), as shown by publication on pravo.gov.ru or kremlin.ru. A signed text with substantially the same powers counts even if renamed. Still a draft, withdrawn or merged into a law: NO.
questions.method: base: judgmental reference class = MoD-drafted presidential decrees put up for public discussion; most are signed, but a minority within ~7-8 weeks of publication; I put that share at 35% (no count yet: method gap to fill). signals: LR 1.2 rising desertion/unauthorised-absence caseload gives the MoD a reason to hurry; LR 1.0 no public statement of a timetable.

history.reason: Opening: draft published 8 Oct (RBC, MK, Izvestia); signing speed is the open question.

questions.title: Will Russia and Ukraine reach a full ceasefire that takes effect by 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if a formal agreement between Russia and Ukraine to halt hostilities along the entire front line is announced by both governments and takes effect between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026. Partial truces (energy-only, sea-only, holiday truces, prisoner-exchange pauses) do not count. Source: official statements of both governments, or two major wire services. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: no full ceasefire in 4.6 years of full-scale war; 0 events, +0.5 smoothing, 83 days. signals: LR 1.5 US proposes trilateral technical talks by end of October; LR 1.3 Miami meeting 9 Oct; LR 0.8 Rubio called a deal 'unachievable', Lavrov hard line; escalation against energy and data centres continues (restraint component 59).

history.reason: Opening: talks about talks, no sign either side accepts a freeze on the current line.

questions.title: Will Russia publicly commit to a reciprocal halt of strikes on energy infrastructure by 20 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 20 Nov 2026 the Kremlin, Russia's president or its foreign ministry publicly states that Russia will stop (or has stopped) striking Ukraine's energy infrastructure as part of a reciprocal arrangement with Ukraine, as reported by two major wire services. Statements by third parties (for example the US president) that both sides agreed do not count without Russia's own confirmation. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: one comparable Russian commitment (the 30-day energy moratorium of March 2025) in 4.6 years; Poisson +0.5 smoothing over 42 days. signals: LR 1.8 Zelensky's public offer of a reciprocal energy truce (22 Sep) and Trump's claim of agreement; LR 0.7 the strike campaign is widening, not narrowing (Omsk, Salavat refineries 8 Oct; Yandex data centres 8-9 Oct); LR 1.2 US-led talks under way.

history.reason: Opening: an offer is on the table but both sides are escalating against each other's infrastructure this week.
Trump announced an energy ceasefire on 11 Oct; Moscow did not confirm and struck Kharkiv and Kyiv power plants within hours. Higher than before only because the US is pushing with offers (NYT).

Peskov 12 Oct: no comment on the energy ceasefire, rejected a 60-day truce, offered only an election-day pause; Russia hit at least six energy targets after Trump's announcement (Zelensky, Reuters 12 Oct).
Kremlin 13.10: contacts on the energy truce continue, no progress (Peskov via Xinhua/Reuters); first night without Russian energy strikes (Reuters 13.10). Still no public commitment.

14.10: mass strike on Ukraine's grid (39 ballistic, 26 energy sites, 600k without power) and Peskov: the truce 'was not specified, so Russia cannot be said to break it' — the opposite of a public commitment. LR x0.65.

questions.title: Will another data centre in Russia be damaged by a drone or missile strike between 10 October and 15 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 15 Nov 2026 a data centre on Russia's internationally recognised territory (other than the Yandex sites at Sasovo, struck 8 Oct, and Kaluga, struck 9 Oct) is damaged by a drone or missile attack, confirmed by its operator or by two major outlets. A repeat strike on Sasovo or Kaluga counts only if reported as new damage on a new date. Debris falling nearby without damage to the facility does not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: reference class = new target classes Ukraine opened during this war (refineries 2024, oil ports, power plants, pumping stations): after two hits in quick succession, a third followed within ~5 weeks in most cases; judgmental 60%. signals: LR 0.8 Yandex hid all four cloud sites from its maps and operators will harden sites; LR 1.2 strikes framed as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres since late September (my Telegram strike collector: 17 Russian-side posts on data-centre strikes on 8 Oct vs baseline 0).

history.reason: Opening: two Yandex sites in two days look like a campaign, not a one-off.

questions.resolution_note: Yandex data centre in Vladimir damaged and halted by drone attack on 11 Oct 2026; confirmed by the operator (Yandex Cloud status channel, via TASS) and reported by Kyiv Independent.

questions.title: Will any NATO member formally request Article 4 consultations between 10 October and 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026 any NATO member formally requests consultations under Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty and NATO confirms it (nato.int press release or Secretary General statement), or two major wire services report the formal request. Calls for 'consultations' without invoking Article 4 do not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: Article 4 requests since Feb 2022 counted as 3 in 4.7 years (Feb 2022; Poland Sep 2025; Estonia Sep 2025); Poisson +0.5 smoothing over 83 days. Checked: NATO's own list ends with Estonia, 23 Sep 2025; none in 2026 so far. signals: LR 1.5 pressure on NATO's eastern flank moved from rhetoric to incidents (Latvia 6 Oct, Lithuania moving troops towards Kaliningrad, Danish PET warnings); LR 1.2 the military component of the Chaos Pulse at 71; LR 0.8 the 2026 incidents so far (German grid sabotage and airport drones, Aug-Sep) were handled bilaterally, without Article 4, so the bar for a request is high.

history.reason: Opening: flank incidents are frequent, but 2026 incidents have not been taken to Article 4.

13.10: third merchant sinking off Bulgaria/Romania in nine days (HS Dignity, 11 missing); Bulgaria asks NATO and EU for surveillance help and summons Russia's ambassador, but Radev says there is no clear evidence to accuse anyone and earlier ruled out Articles 4 and 5 (Stars and Stripes, RBC-Ukraine 13.10).

Bulgaria (Radev to parliament 14.10, AP): Russia 'likely' behind 4 ship attacks, 2 sunk, but cannot prove it; asks NATO for counter-drone support, not Art.4. Romania: drone briefly entered airspace near Sulina, F-16s scrambled (MApN 14.10). LR x1.15.

First drone strike on a ship inside a NATO member's territorial waters: Romania's president says the Wine Trader (8 missing) and Yara J were hit by drones and promises a reaction; a drone entered Romanian airspace; Rutte met Dan and Radev. No Article 4 request yet. bayes x1.5. Crowd (32%) was visible before this update.

16.10: Romania's FM put full responsibility on Russia and allies agreed to convene the North Atlantic Council within days without Article 4 (Politico, Kyiv Post 16.10). An NAC meeting is the substitute path chosen; attacks continue, so only a small cut. LR 0.9 on 0.30.

questions.title: Will the US strike targets on Iranian territory before the US midterm elections (10 Oct - 2 Nov 2026)?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 2 Nov 2026 (UTC) US military forces strike targets on Iran's land territory or in Iran's territorial waters, as confirmed by the US government or two major wire services. Strikes on Iranian proxies outside Iran, on Iranian ships in international waters, interceptions of missiles or drones, and Israeli-only strikes do not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: reference class = the current Pakistan-brokered US-Iran ceasefire, ~180 days with no US strike on Iranian territory (strikes on tankers in Sep were at sea); 0 events in 0.5 years, +0.5 smoothing, 24 days. signals: LR 0.5 Trump publicly promised no strikes before the 3 Nov midterms (AP, Guardian, 8 Oct); LR 1.3 Pentagon reportedly told to prepare options; LR 1.3 near-nightly IRGC attacks on Hormuz shipping since 29 Sep.

history.reason: Opening: an explicit presidential promise with an electoral motive covers the whole window.

questions.title: Will 100 or more ships cross the Strait of Hormuz on a single day by 31 December 2026, per IMF PortWatch?
questions.criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch daily transit-call data for the Strait of Hormuz shows 100 or more transits on any single day between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026 (data as published by 15 Jan 2027). Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: reference class = major chokepoint disruptions by an armed party (Bab el-Mandeb 2024-25, Hormuz 2026): a return to normal daily traffic within ~3 months of a still-active attack campaign is rare; judgmental 8%. signals: LR 0.8 Trump rejected Iran's 7-day reopening proposal; LR 0.7 IRGC attacks vessels nearly nightly (my transit signal: 2.7/day vs 3 baseline, Oct 8); LR 1.2 Iran says reopening would begin the day Washington accepts its plan, and Iran's economy is under acute strain.

history.reason: Opening: traffic is ~3 ships a day; a deal would have to come fast and stick.

questions.title: Will the Brent spot price be above $130 per barrel on 30 October 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if the EIA Europe Brent spot price FOB (series RBRTE) for 30 Oct 2026 is above $130.00. If no price is published for that date, the last published price before it decides. Source: EIA (eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/RBRTED.htm) or FRED DCOILBRENTEU. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: trend: lognormal, zero drift, from $125.44 (EIA spot, 7-8 Oct), annualised volatility 0.75 = realised volatility of my 30-day spot series (daily sd 4.8%), 21 days. base: empirical: in my 30-day history spot was above $130 on about a third of days since mid-September; 45% as a crude outside view. signals: LR 0.9 Trump's no-strike promise removes the main upside tail before 3 Nov; LR 1.1 nightly attacks keep Hormuz shut.

history.reason: Opening: spot sits just under the line with very high volatility.

questions.title: Will the Brent spot price be below $100 per barrel on 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if the EIA Europe Brent spot price FOB (series RBRTE) for 31 Dec 2026 is below $100.00; if none is published that day, the last price before it decides. Source: EIA or FRED DCOILBRENTEU. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: trend: lognormal, zero drift, from $125.44, annual volatility 0.75, 83 days. base: judgmental 25%: a 20% fall needs a Hormuz reopening or demand destruction; in 2022 Brent fell from $120+ to under $100 within ~3 months of its peak. signals: LR 0.8 no reopening deal in sight, attacks continue; LR 1.2 demand destruction and IEA stock releases (~100 mb) plus Saudi East-West pipeline at 5.8 mb/d.

history.reason: Opening: a fall below $100 requires a political event; volatility makes it far from impossible.

questions.title: Will a Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement be announced by 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026 Saudi Arabia and the Houthis (Ansar Allah), directly or through a mediator such as Oman or the UN, announce an agreed ceasefire or truce covering cross-border strikes, confirmed by both sides or by the mediator and two major wire services. Unilateral pauses do not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: Saudi-Houthi war 2015-2026: formal truces in 2016 and 2022 (2 in ~11 years) but rounds of open fighting are often followed by mediated truces within months; judgmental 15% for 12 weeks. signals: LR 0.8 Saudi Arabia is preparing an assault to break the Red Sea chokehold (Reuters 2 Oct) and Mecca Pact allies (Pakistan, Turkey) are arming it; LR 0.7 first Saudi deaths 7 Oct and attacks on Riyadh airport 9 Oct raise the cost of a quick truce.

history.reason: AFP (9 Oct, one regional source): Saudi Arabia will not accept a truce until the government regains lost territory; the coalition vows a 'firm' response after 3 deaths at Riyadh airport. LR 0.85, single anonymous source so a small step.
Third Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in a week (10 Oct), terminal hit; Saudi Arabia still rejects a truce before regaining territory; ground offensive ongoing.

First reported Saudi-Iranian FM call since the escalation (11 Oct) and Iran's public offer to broker Saudi-Houthi talks (Baghaei 12 Oct); Houthi missiles at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait continued 12 Oct.

questions.title: Will the US Federal Reserve raise rates at its 27-28 October 2026 meeting?
questions.criteria: YES if the FOMC statement of 28 Oct 2026 raises the federal funds target range above 3.75-4.00%. Unchanged or lower: NO. Source: federalreserve.gov.
questions.method: base: reference class = the meeting right after the first hike of a cycle (2004: hike, 2015: no, 2022: hike, 1999: no); about half; 45%. signals: LR 0.6 Governor Waller (8 Oct) left the door open to a pause; LR 0.6 weak September payrolls (+29k, unemployment 4.2%); LR 1.2 core PCE 3%, energy shock. Honesty note: a search snippet summarising market pricing was visible before I wrote this number, so this question's errata-vs-crowd comparison is contaminated.

history.reason: Opening: the committee signalled one more hike this year; December looks likelier than October.

CPI Sep (BLS 14.10): 3.7% y/y, core 2.6%, both above consensus; 10y at 5.3%, 10y auction highest yield in 26 years (WSJ). LR x1.6 on 0.35 -> 0.46, rounded down. Crowd/market pricing (~50% per Trading Economics) seen before this update — said openly.

questions.title: Will the Bank of Russia raise its key rate above 14% on 23 October 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if the Bank of Russia board decision of 23 Oct 2026 sets the key rate above 14.00%. Unchanged or lower: NO. Source: cbr.ru press release.
questions.method: base: reference class = Bank of Russia meetings right after it paused an easing cycle (2017-2025): reversals to a hike at the next meeting are rare, about 1 in 10. signals: LR 1.5 underlying inflation re-accelerated to 5-6% annualised, fuel shortages, second-round effects, possible bigger budget deficit; LR 0.8 Nabiullina framed September as a 'pause' in cutting, not a turn.

history.reason: Opening: the pause leaves a hold as the default; a hike needs a bad inflation print or a budget shock.

questions.title: Will the official rouble rate be weaker than 90 per US dollar on 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if the Bank of Russia official USD/RUB rate set for 31 Dec 2026 is above 90.00 roubles per dollar. Source: cbr.ru daily rates. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: trend: lognormal, zero drift, from 85.42 (CBR, 8 Oct), annualised volatility 0.18 (rouble's typical 2024-26 range), 83 days. base: judgmental 25% (year-end seasonal import demand historically weakens the rouble). signals: LR 1.1 fuel imports and export bottlenecks weakened the rouble over summer (Nabiullina); LR 0.9 oil above $120 supports export revenue.

history.reason: Opening: 5% weaker in under three months is a normal-size move for the rouble.

questions.title: Will Likud win the most seats in Israel's 27 October 2026 Knesset election?
questions.criteria: YES if, in the official results certified by Israel's Central Elections Committee, Likud wins more seats than any other list. A tie for first place: NO. If the election is postponed beyond 31 Dec 2026 the question is annulled. Source: votes26.bechirot.gov.il or two major outlets reporting the certified result.
questions.method: trend: polling average (latest poll from each of 8 outlets, israel.com tracker of 8 Oct) Likud 22.5 vs Yashar 21.6; normal error on the lead with sd 3 seats -> P(lead > 0). base: in Israeli elections since 2009 the party leading the final polling average won most seats in most cases, but leads under 1 seat were coin-flips; 60%.

history.reason: Opening: a sub-one-seat lead 18 days out.

questions.title: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be sworn in as prime minister of the next Israeli government by 30 April 2027?
questions.criteria: YES if a new Israeli government formed after the 27 Oct 2026 election, with Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister, wins a Knesset confidence vote and is sworn in by 30 Apr 2027. NO if another person is sworn in, or no new government is sworn in by that date (continuing as caretaker prime minister does not count). Source: Knesset website or two major outlets.
questions.method: base: his outgoing coalition averages 51.6 seats, 9.4 short of 61 (8-outlet average, 8 Oct; only Channel 14 shows 61+); reference class = Israeli elections where the incumbent bloc polled 5+ seats short three weeks out (2019 x2, 2021): the incumbent did not form a new government in any, but 2022 shows late shifts; judgmental 25%. signals: LR 1.1 Likud still the largest list; LR 1.3 the opposition needs Arab parties or Yisrael Beiteinu plus Haredi defections, which has failed before, and repeat elections would leave him as caretaker (NO here).

history.reason: Opening: polls say no majority; coalition arithmetic on the other side is hard too.

questions.title: Will Russia officially announce a new mobilisation of reservists by 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026 (Moscow time) a presidential decree or an official announcement by the Russian president or government declares a mobilisation (partial or general) of reservists, as published on kremlin.ru / pravo.gov.ru or reported by two major wire services. Pre-mortem: a battlefield shock or a failed US-led track by December; plausible but not visible now. second: independent estimate by Claude Fable 5.1, given the question, criteria and evidence but not my number (9 Oct 2026).

history.reason: Opening: the state is building mobilisation-without-declaration; a decree would need a shock.

MRI report 11 Oct: index 54 -> 55. Signals model: LR 1.1 Miami talks ended early with no result and Russia reportedly holds to 'all objectives' (part of my pre-mortem path, one-sided report); LR 1.05 two draft documents extend the machinery (women's reserve age bill 8108-9, military police search decree draft). Signals 0.06 -> 0.069; ensemble stays 0.07. No decree, no mass reservist summons.

MRI 14 Oct: 55, unchanged. Kept at 7%: recruitment steady (Kluge, Sept 29.9k), cost per recruit +30% y/y and bonuses stagnating at Q4 start push slowly up; energy-truce contacts and US pressure on Kyiv lower near-term motive. No threshold event.

questions.title: Will the US strike targets on Iranian territory between 3 November and 31 December 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 3 Nov and 31 Dec 2026 (UTC) US military forces strike targets on Iran's land territory or in Iran's territorial waters, as confirmed by the US government or two major wire services. Strikes on Iranian proxies outside Iran, on Iranian ships in international waters, interceptions, and Israeli-only strikes do not count. Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: the current US-Iran ceasefire, ~180 days with no US strike on Iranian territory; 0 events in 0.5 years, +0.5 smoothing, 58 days. signals: LR 2.0 Trump tied the pause explicitly to the midterms and called stronger strikes 'possible' afterwards (Time; AP 8 Oct); LR 1.3 Pentagon told to prepare options; LR 1.3 near-nightly IRGC attacks on shipping and the Sep 9 missile strike on a US base in Jordan; LR 0.8 Iran's economic distress makes a deal more likely. second: independent estimate by Claude Fable 5.1, given the question, criteria and evidence but not my number (9 Oct 2026). Fable is much higher than my models (55% vs my 15% and 32%): it weighs the explicitly electoral framing of the pause; I keep equal weights and let the score decide.

history.reason: Opening: the promise expires on 3 Nov and nothing has been settled.

questions.title: Will Strait of Hormuz traffic recover to a 7-day average of at least 20 transits a day by 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch data for the Strait of Hormuz shows a 7-day moving average of at least 20 daily transit calls on any day between 10 Oct and 30 Nov 2026 (as published by 10 Dec 2026). Otherwise NO.
questions.method: base: politically closed chokepoints under an active attack campaign rarely recover fast (Red Sea traffic stayed depressed for over a year); 20/day is still only ~20% of normal, so a deal would clear it quickly; judgmental 15%. signals: LR 0.8 Trump rejected Iran's 7-day reopening proposal; LR 1.2 Iran offered reopening and the closure throttles its own revenue amid a currency collapse; LR 0.8 IRGC attacks nearly nightly since 29 Sep (my transit signal 2.7/day, 8 Oct). second: independent estimate by Claude Fable 5.1, given the question, criteria and evidence but not my number (9 Oct 2026).

history.reason: Kpler (via CNBC/Dawn, 9 Oct): 7 transits on 6 Oct, a two-month low, Hormuz exports -40% vs pre-war; IRGC now threatens ships on 'unauthorised routes' across the whole region. LR 0.85 on the prior 16%.
Iran calls the US reply insufficient and says it is no longer responding (Rezaei, 11 Oct); tankers hit 10-11 Oct.

questions.title: Will Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport be closed to commercial flights for at least 24 consecutive hours between 11 and 31 October 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if GACA, the airport operator, or at least two major outlets (AP, Reuters, AFP, Bloomberg) report that all commercial flight operations at King Khalid International Airport (RUH) were suspended for a continuous period of 24 hours or more starting between 11 Oct and 31 Oct 2026 (UTC). Suspensions of single airlines or terminals do not count. NO otherwise.
questions.method: base: rare full-day closures of Gulf capital airports in this war (judgement, no clean series); signals: bayes x2 (three strikes in a week, terminal hit) x0.8 (quick reopenings so far)

history.reason: Third hit on the airport in a week; on 10 Oct a missile struck the domestic terminal complex and GACA suspended operations temporarily. So far reopenings came within hours.

AP 11 Oct: airport still closed on Sunday after the 10 Oct strike (12 dead, 309 injured), terminal hit again on 11 Oct. If the closure lasts past 00:00 UTC 12 Oct, a 24h window starting 11 Oct is met; awaiting confirmation.

GACA (SPA, 12 Oct 08:35 GMT) extended the suspension of operations; AeroCorner: still closed at 03:58 UTC 12 Oct; Aerospace Global News reports a NOTAM closing RUH until at least 17 Oct. Not resolved yet: Cirium shows one flight operated on 11 Oct and FlightAware logged delays, so 'all operations suspended for 24h' needs a clean window; recheck 13 Oct.

questions.resolution_note: GACA (SPA 12.10 08:35 GMT, https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2699133) extended the suspension of operations; Reuters 13.10 (via Pajhwok): closed since 10.10, closure extended to 21:00 GMT 17.10. Any 24h window from 12.10 00:00 UTC lies inside an official all-operations suspension. Caveat: Cirium showed >=1 departure on 11.10; a single travel site claims limited Saudia domestic flights from 13.10 (not confirmed by GACA or wires).

questions.title: Will the United States carry out acknowledged military strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen by 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if the US government (White House, Pentagon, CENTCOM) confirms US forces struck Houthi targets in Yemen between 11 Oct and 30 Nov 2026, or at least two major outlets report such US strikes as fact citing US officials. Intelligence, refuelling or support for Saudi strikes does not count. NO otherwise.
questions.method: base: forecast calc rate, 2 US anti-Houthi campaigns in 3 years over 51 days = 0.11; signals: bayes x3 (Trump 'may') x1.3 (support already flowing); trend: judgement; ensemble ~0.27

history.reason: Trump said on 10 Oct the US 'may' join strikes after the Riyadh airport attacks; the US already gives intelligence and refuelling (Al-Monitor). No decision announced; pre-midterm caution.
A US citizen was killed in the 10 Oct Riyadh airport strike; Trump says the US may join Saudi strikes and will decide very quickly.

questions.title: Will the United States suspend intelligence sharing with Ukraine by 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if between 11 Oct and 30 Nov 2026 a US official confirms on the record, or at least two major outlets (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, FT, NYT, WSJ, Axios) report as implemented, a suspension or pause (full or covering long-range targeting) of US intelligence sharing with Ukraine. A threat or warning does not count. NO otherwise.
questions.method: base: forecast calc rate, 1 suspension in 2 years over 51 days = 0.10; signals: bayes x2.5 (reported threat) x1.2 (Trump vs Zelensky), shaded down for the official denial

history.reason: Axios and FT (10 Oct) report Witkoff and Kushner threatened to cut intelligence over refinery strikes; a US official denies a threat was made. Trump called for Ukraine to get a new president. Precedent: a pause in March 2025.
Threat to cut intelligence sharing now confirmed by two Ukrainian officials (Kyiv Independent 12 Oct), tied to refinery strikes; but Kyiv is complying for now, which lowers the trigger.

Zelensky (AP, FT 15 Oct) says Ukraine has been denied the usual intelligence on Russian ballistic launches and calls the withdrawal dangerous; Ukrainian defence officials confirm the US threat. Trump says sharing has not stopped; no US official or two outlets report a suspension as implemented, so not YES. bayes x1.9.

16.10: Trump calls renewed refinery strikes a 'disgrace' (Reuters/BBC), White House reportedly ordered Starshield restrictions in Ukraine (Reuters via UP), ammunition sales to allies paused (Newsmax). Pressure toolkit is being used step by step; LR 1.25 on 0.29.

questions.title: Will there be a pause of at least 14 consecutive days without a Ukrainian strike on a Russian oil refinery between 11 October and 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if there is any window of 14 consecutive UTC days within 11 Oct - 30 Nov 2026 in which no strike on a Russian oil refinery is reported as carried out by Ukraine by Ukraine's General Staff, the Ukrainian president, or at least two major outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Moscow Times). Strikes on depots, pumping stations or terminals do not count. NO otherwise.
questions.method: base: judgement from 2025-26 campaign which had multi-week lulls a few times a year; signals: bayes x1.5 (US pressure) x0.6 (Kyiv's stated refusal; Russia keeps striking the grid)

history.reason: US pressure (intelligence threat, diesel deal) pushes for a halt; Kyiv says it will keep 'burning refineries' unless Russia stops striking Ukraine's grid. Campaign at its normal pace (6 sites in 7 days vs norm 6.8).
Zelensky publicly ready to stop strikes on Russian energy if Russia reciprocates; Russia kept striking, so a pause still unlikely.

Zelensky: armed forces received orders, no Russian refinery was hit on the night of 11-12 Oct (Moscow Times, Kyiv Independent); Kyiv Independent (two Ukrainian officials): US threatened to cut intelligence sharing and PURL if refineries are hit. Pause is conditional on Russian reciprocity, which has not come (6 energy targets hit, Zelensky 12 Oct).

Zelensky 13.10: two days without Ukrainian refinery strikes; Reuters 13.10: Russia hit no energy targets overnight for the first time since the truce claim. Pause is holding so far but has no Russian commitment; 12 more days needed.

Ukraine's pause is day 3 (Lytvyn 14.10 denies refinery strikes; Novak claims Saratov and Ryazan were hit), but Russia did not reciprocate and Kyiv threatens large-scale winter strikes; the incentive to keep the pause 14 days fell. LR x0.8.

The pause ended after 3 days: Ukraine hit the Ryazan refinery on 15 Oct (governor, Russian MoD, a senior Ukrainian official to AP) and Zelensky told the FT the block is lifted. A 14-day window now needs a new pause, against Kyiv's stated position. bayes x0.4.

questions.title: Will the State Duma pass bill No. 8108-9 (raising women's military service and reserve age limits) in the first reading by 30 November 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if by 30 Nov 2026 (Moscow time) the State Duma adopts government bill No. 8108-9 (amendments to the law on military duty and military service raising the service age limit for women from 45 to 50 and their reserve age limits) in the first reading, as shown on sozd.duma.gov.ru or reported by two major Russian news agencies. NO if not adopted in first reading by then, including withdrawal or rejection. A merged or renumbered bill with the same content counts.
questions.method: base: reference class = government bills on military service introduced to the Duma, share passing first reading within about 7 weeks of introduction; my rough estimate from the 2023-2025 pattern of such bills (often fast-tracked) about 0.55, not a counted sample. signals: LR 1.2 government/MoD bill framed as social guarantees, uncontroversial in the Duma; LR 0.85 the autumn session is crowded with the 2027-2029 budget. No crowd market.

history.reason: Opened from the MRI report of 11 Oct: the bill was introduced on 9 Oct; first reading would be the next observable step of the legal-readiness component. Pre-mortem (it is 30 Nov and I was wrong): the Duma prioritised the budget and scheduled the bill for December, or it was sent back for revision after public attention to the mobilisation side effect.

questions.title: Will Egypt's House of Representatives approve an authorisation for military action to defend Saudi Arabia by 25 October 2026?
questions.criteria: YES if Egypt's House of Representatives adopts, by 25 Oct 2026 23:59 UTC, a resolution or vote authorising the president to deploy or use armed forces in defence of Saudi Arabia (conditional on a Saudi request counts). A statement of support without authorisation, or a deferral, is NO. Source: Ahram, Reuters, AFP or the House.
questions.method: Batch 17.10: my number written before asking Claude Fable blind (it never saw mine); ensemble = log-odds mean of base and the two judgements.

history.reason: Sisi asked for an emergency session on 17 Oct; plenary set for 18 Oct; the House approved past security requests (Libya 2020 unanimously). Residual risk: a support statement short of authorisation.
18.10: parliament debated but postponed the vote to 19.10 (MEE citing Reuters); delay, not rejection

19.10: House adjourned the mandate session a second time; Reuters (via Straits Times 19.10) says the vote is expected next week, Arabic outlets (alsaudi.news, Roayah 19.10) say discussions resume 26.10, after the 25.10 deadline. AFP (via SOFX) said deliberations continue Tuesday 20.10, so an early vote is not excluded.

questions.criteria: YES if by 31 Oct 2026 US CENTCOM or UKMTO publicly states that a merchant vessel struck a sea mine (or 'mine') in or near the Strait of Hormuz in an incident dated 17 Oct 2026 or later. Correction to my own update an hour earlier: I wrote '~7 episodes, Laplace 0/7'.
